answer: A proof-of-burn protocol deters Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to destroy cryptocurrency to a sable address before registering its network vertex. To filter a gale of synthetic identities, the network only accepts transactions certified by verifiable burn proofs. An attacker must sacrifice scarce liquid capital per simulated node. However, well-funded adversaries can still afford mass identity creation, and the entry cost excludes capital-constrained agents.
